question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient starts bleeding heavily right after birth?

options.A: Massage the uterus and call for emergency assistance
options.B: Wait for laboratory results before taking any action
options.C: Send the patient home to rest in bed
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Act fast! Massaging the uterus makes it clamp down and stop the bleeding, while shouting for help brings your team running.

question: A patient having radiation for breast cancer asks if she can wear her tight underwire bra. What should you say?

options.A: Yes, as long as it is washed in hot water
options.B: Yes, underwire provides necessary support during healing
options.C: No, choose a soft, loose-fitting garment to avoid friction on the skin
options.D: Only wear it during the actual radiation treatment session

explanation: Tight clothing rubs against fragile skin and causes irritation. Recommending soft, loose clothes keeps your patient comfortable!

question: Which body part connects the back of the nose and mouth to the voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Bronchus
options.B: Trachea
options.C: Alveoli
options.D: Pharynx

explanation: The pharynx is simply the muscular tube right behind your mouth and nasal cavity that acts as a highway, guiding air down toward your larynx and lungs.

question: What is usually the very first sign that a newborn is developing tetanus?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Inability to suck or feed properly
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: High fever and watery diarrhea

explanation: Correct! Stiff jaw muscles make it hard for the baby to latch or suck, which is often the first warning sign mothers and nurses notice.

question: During a CT scan with contrast, a patient suddenly develops widespread hives, facial swelling, and mild wheezing. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Ask the patient to hold their breath until the scanning is finished.
options.B: Stop the contrast injection and notify the medical team immediately.
options.C: Reassure the patient that hives are a completely normal side effect.
options.D: Administer a dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient.

explanation: Hives and wheezing indicate an allergic reaction to the contrast media, requiring the immediate cessation of the infusion and prompt emergency medical intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why does a rehab nurse encourage a patient to do tasks slowly by themselves instead of rushing to help?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the nursing staff
options.B: To test the physical strength of the patient
options.C: To build patient independence and self-reliance
options.D: To lower hospital operational costs

explanation: Rehab is all about empowerment! Letting patients do things on their own helps them rebuild their confidence and skills. Great nursing insight!

question: When starting an eye irrigation, where do you aim the stream of fluid?

options.A: Directly onto the center of the black pupil
options.B: At the outer corner, flowing inward toward the nose
options.C: Directly against the upper eyelid skin
options.D: At the inner canthus, flowing toward the outer canthus

explanation: Always flow from the inside corner (near the nose) toward the outside corner. This follows natural tear flow and keeps junk out of the tear ducts!

question: Which chemical messengers in the brain usually get thrown out of balance during neurodegeneration?

options.A: Blood proteins like albumin and globulin
options.B: Neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin
options.C: Digestive enzymes like pepsin and amylase
options.D: Respiratory gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide

explanation: Spot on! When brain cells die off, it messes up neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin, which directly change mood, behavior, and thinking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h2)

question: Right after the placenta is safely delivered, what is your next immediate nursing action?

options.A: Massage the uterine fundus to ensure it remains firm and contracted
options.B: Transfer the mother immediately to the operating theatre for suturing
options.C: Check the newborn's vital signs and complete the Apgar scoring chart
options.D: Administer a second dose of IV fluids containing magnesium sulfate

explanation: Give that fundus a gentle massage! It wakes up the muscle fibers so they squeeze shut on open blood vessels, stopping postpartum hemorrhage in its tracks.

question: How is 'low vision' best described in a clinical setting?

options.A: Total, permanent blindness with zero light perception
options.B: Vision loss that cannot be fully fixed with regular glasses, medicine, or surgery
options.C: A temporary blur from eye strain or tiredness
options.D: Simple nearsightedness that is easily corrected with prescription lenses

explanation: Low vision means standard glasses or medical treatments can't bring sight back to normal, even though the person still has some helpful vision left.

question: Which strategy helps a nurse prevent burnout when dealing with frequent patient losses?

options.A: Suppressing all feelings of sadness so nobody notices
options.B: Avoiding all patients who have terminal diagnoses
options.C: Participating in regular team debriefings and setting emotional boundaries
options.D: Working extra double shifts to stay distracted

explanation: Talking through tough losses with colleagues and keeping healthy boundaries protects your mental health and keeps your caring spirit strong!

question: Why do certain medications need to be taken strictly on an empty stomach?

options.A: To ensure the liver enzymes are completely deactivated during digestion
options.B: To speed up the digestive process in the large intestine
options.C: To increase the overall acidity of the liver portal system
options.D: To prevent food from binding to the drug or delaying its absorption

explanation: Some foods love to mess with medications by chemically binding to them or slowing down how fast the stomach empties, which changes how much medicine actually gets into the blood.

question: Why is foetal scalp blood sampling sometimes performed when a CTG is abnormal?

options.A: To check the actual acid-base balance and confirm true oxygen shortage
options.B: To deliver pain medication directly through the baby's scalp skin
options.C: To stimulate the baby to move away from the umbilical cord
options.D: To collect a DNA sample for genetic screening after birth

explanation: Scalp blood testing measures pH levels to see if the baby is developing dangerous acidosis from lack of oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h4)

question: Which of these is classified as 'sharps' waste?

options.A: Hypodermic needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Disposable paper bed sheets
options.C: Cotton wool balls and surgical gauze
options.D: Plastic IV fluid bags and tubing

explanation: Easy and clear! Needles and blades have sharp edges that can puncture skin, so they need special handling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why is it helpful to feel (palpate) the patient's lower belly before doing a catheterisation?

options.A: To stimulate the urethral sphincter to open
options.B: To check if the kidneys are infected
options.C: To measure the exact length of the urethra
options.D: To confirm the presence of a full, distended bladder

explanation: Spot on! Feeling the lower belly (suprapubic area) lets you check if urine is actually backed up and trapped in the bladder, confirming you really need to catheterize.

question: How was traditional West African pharmacological knowledge primarily preserved and transmitted?

options.A: Through oral tradition passed down generations
options.B: Through printed textbooks distributed to apprentices
options.C: Via ancient stone tablets stored in royal palaces
options.D: Via detailed digital databases kept by village elders

explanation: Indigenous medicinal knowledge in West Africa was historically preserved and handed down by word of mouth from older healers to younger apprentices. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h2)

question: A patient comes in with acute diverticulitis and severe lower left belly pain. Which diet order is best for this acute stage?

options.A: High-protein liquid supplement drinks
options.B: Clear liquids to let the bowel rest
options.C: High-fiber diet with extra raw vegetables
options.D: Regular solid food with high roughage

explanation: You got it! When diverticulitis flares up, the inflamed colon needs a break. Clear liquids help give the bowel time to rest and heal.

question: How do joints usually get affected in rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: Restricted entirely to the spinal column
options.B: Limited to a single weight-bearing joint
options.C: Symmetrical across both sides of the body
options.D: Randomly scattered without any clear pattern

explanation: A classic sign of rheumatoid arthritis is symmetry! If the left wrist or knee hurts, the right one is usually acting up in the exact same way.

question: As a nurse working in adolescent health, which of these actions should you definitely NOT do?

options.A: Sharing a teenager's private health details with their neighbors
options.B: Screening for risky behaviors in a supportive, private setting
options.C: Providing confidential counseling on sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Educating on the correct use of modern contraceptive methods

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred! Gossiping or sharing private health info breaks professional ethics and destroys patient trust immediately.

question: According to Piaget, which stage of thinking do teenagers enter?

options.A: Concrete operational stage
options.B: Preoperational stage
options.C: Formal operational stage
options.D: Sensorimotor stage

explanation: Correct! Teens enter the formal operational stage, where they start mastering abstract thinking and complex problem-solving.

question: What common farming practice greatly increases the spread of Taenia solium in rural areas?

options.A: Keeping pigs strictly indoors in concrete pens with automated cleaning
options.B: Free-range scavenging of pigs where human waste is accessible
options.C: Vaccinating all livestock against bacterial infections yearly
options.D: Feeding cattle exclusively on imported commercial grain

explanation: That's right! When pigs roam about freely and have access to human faeces where open defecation occurs, they easily pick up tapeworm eggs.

question: What must a nurse always do before starting any care in a patient's home?

options.A: Publishing the care plan in a national newspaper
options.B: Receiving written approval from local community leaders
options.C: Consulting the hospital board of directors
options.D: Obtaining proper informed consent from the patient

explanation: Always! Respecting our patients means getting their clear okay before doing any checks or procedures.

question: How should a scrubbed nurse enter the operating room after finishing their scrub?

options.A: Back through the door to keep hands safe and away from clothing
options.B: Ask an unscrubbed colleague to open the door and pull them in
options.C: Push the door open while keeping hands high near the face
options.D: Turn sideways and slide through a narrow opening

explanation: Backing in ensures your front and clean hands don't accidentally brush against the door or your scrubs.

question: What is the main problem happening in all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion and oxygen delivery
options.B: Elevated blood sugar levels in the bloodstream
options.C: Sudden swelling of the upper respiratory tract
options.D: High fever caused by a bacterial infection

explanation: Simply put, shock means the body's tissues aren't getting enough blood and oxygen to survive and do their work.

question: How does long-term high blood pressure in the lungs (pulmonary hypertension) directly change the heart?

options.A: It shrinks the left atrium because less blood returns from the lungs
options.B: It causes the heart valves to stretch and leak due to low blood pressure
options.C: It weakens the left ventricle by reducing blood flow through the aorta
options.D: It causes the right ventricle to thicken and enlarge from working too hard

explanation: You've got it! Just like lifting heavy weights makes a bicep grow, the right ventricle bulks up (hypertrophies) when it has to push against high lung pressures. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which part of the adolescent brain matures faster, leading to reward-seeking and impulsive behavior?

options.A: The limbic system
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The prefrontal cortex
options.D: The brainstem

explanation: The limbic system develops early during puberty, driving strong emotions and a desire for immediate rewards before the logical reasoning centers are fully mature. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which type of questioning helps an anxious PAC patient share their story comfortably?

options.A: Closed yes-or-no prompts
options.B: Open-ended questions
options.C: Leading legal inquiries
options.D: Rapid fire interrogation

explanation: Asking questions like 'How have you been feeling since yesterday?' lets patients talk in their own words without feeling cornered.

question: A patient at a local clinic says they want to stop their modern epilepsy drugs and use unverified traditional herbs instead. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain the risks of stopping medication abruptly and discuss how to safely manage the condition together
options.B: Threaten to report the patient to local authorities if they miss a single clinic appointment
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication immediately to see what happens
options.D: Tell the patient that traditional remedies are completely harmless and can replace drugs

explanation: Always meet patients with empathy and respect. Instead of judging, gently educate them on why stopping their meds is dangerous while working together to support their overall health journey.

question: What emergency procedure is used to drain extra fluid from around the heart during cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Thoracentesis
options.B: Cardioversion
options.C: Pericardiocentesis
options.D: Paracentesis

explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves gently passing a needle into the pericardial sac to draw out fluid and relieve dangerous pressure on the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is getting enough sleep so important for our patients in the hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will be discharged within forty-eight hours
options.B: It eliminates the need for expensive pain relief medications
options.C: It prevents patients from talking too much to the nursing staff
options.D: It speeds up physical healing and strengthens the body's immune defenses

explanation: When patients sleep well, their bodies can focus on repairing tissues and fighting off infections. Good rest is a powerful form of medicine!

question: What is your duty as a nurse regarding a patient's feelings and mindset during a referral?

options.A: Counseling the patient to address fears and explain why care is needed
options.B: Telling the family to ignore advice given by the receiving doctor
options.C: Forcing the patient to leave the clinic immediately without explanation
options.D: Convincing the patient that the local clinic can handle everything

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Taking time to talk, soothe fears, and explain things helps the patient trust the process and actually go for their treatment.

question: A mum in labour is very frightened and tense, and her labour is slowing down even though her contractions are strong. Which of the Four Ps is playing a role here?

options.A: Psyche
options.B: Passage
options.C: Passenger
options.D: Power

explanation: Fear and anxiety relate to the 'psyche'! Stress hormones can slow things down, so reassuring your patient is a big part of nursing care.

question: What is the usual gas flow rate range set on the flowmeter for a standard compressor nebulizer?

options.A: 20 to 25 liters per minute
options.B: 12 to 15 liters per minute
options.C: 6 to 8 liters per minute
options.D: 1 to 2 liters per minute
